source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design — Agriculture and Nutrition, Grade 7
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (no pages param). First published 2022, Revised 2024. Backfilled retroactively — skills already shipped in web/src/skills/agricultureG7/ before this record was written. 4 strands: 1.0 Conservation of Resources, 2.0 Food Production Processes, 3.0 Hygiene Practices, 4.0 Production Techniques. Sub-strand 2.4's full body-text name is 'Cooking: Grilling, Roasting and Steaming' — the front-matter Summary of Strands and Sub Strands table abbreviates it to 'Cooking: Roasting and steaming', omitting Grilling; the body text (which also names grilling explicitly in its outcomes and learning experiences) is treated as authoritative.

subStrands.name: 1.1 Controlling Soil Pollution
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the causes of soil pollution in gardening
control soil pollution in home environment
demonstrate responsibility in using safe farming practices to conserve the soil
keyInquiryQuestions: How can household practices cause soil pollution?
learningExperiences: search and watch a video clip or print media on causes of soil pollution and then share experiences on causes of soil pollution such as waste water, excessive use of artificial fertilizers, agricultural chemicals and plastic wastes
engage in safe soil pollution control practices such as safe disposal of household waste water, used chemical containers and plastic wastes

create awareness messages against improper disposal of waste water, dumping of soil pollutants, used chemical containers and plastic wastes and use of correct types and amounts of farm chemicals and fertilizers
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science: relating soil pollution to other forms of environmental pollution.

subStrands.name: 1.2 Constructing Water Retention Structures
specificLearningOutcomes: describe how surface run-off can be used in gardening
construct water retention structures to conserve surface runoff
adopt utilization of surface run-off in gardening
keyInquiryQuestions: How can surface run-off be conserved for gardening purposes?
How does construction of water retention structures conserve water?
learningExperiences: search for information and discuss how surface run-off can be conserved in structures such as water retention ditches and water retention pits for gardening
construct retention ditches or retention pits for water conservation and establish a crop of their choice such as a banana sucker, sugarcane, napier grass or arrowroot
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: destruction of environment by excess water in socio-economic amenities.

subStrands.name: 1.3 Conserving Food Nutrients
specificLearningOutcomes: identify ways of conserving vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables
conserve vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables
adopt conservation of vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables
keyInquiryQuestions: How do we conserve vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables?
learningExperiences: search for information and discuss ways of conserving vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables such as washing, peeling, cutting, cooking time, and covering
conserve vitamins and mineral salts in vegetables during food handling, preparation and cooking
adopt appropriate ways of handling, preparing and cooking vegetables to conserve vitamins and mineral salts
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science: healthy growth and development.

subStrands.name: 1.4 Growing Trees
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the importance of trees in conserving the environment
plant trees to conserve the environment
adopt tree planting as a way of conserving the environment
keyInquiryQuestions: How can growing of trees conserve the environment?
learningExperiences: search for information on importance of trees and make presentations in class to share their findings
plant at least one tree either from seeds, or seedlings or cuttings and take care of the seedling until it is fully established
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: conservation of natural resources.

subStrands.name: 2.1 Preparing Planting Site and Establishing Crop
specificLearningOutcomes: determine appropriate tilth for selected planting material
prepare a suitable tilth for establishing selected planting material
adopt appropriate tilth in establishing a selected planting material
keyInquiryQuestions: How does planting material determine planting site preparation?
learningExperiences: observe provided planting materials and suggest appropriate tilth for each material (small sized seeds for fine tilth, medium sized seeds for medium tilth and large planting materials like tubers, suckers and cuttings for coarse tilth)
prepare suitable sites (fine tilth for small seeds, medium tilth for medium sized seeds, coarse tilth for large planting materials like tubers, suckers and cuttings)
establish a planting material of their choice in the selected soil tilth
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science: relating planting site (tilth) and seed size to the concept of germination.

subStrands.name: 2.2 Selected Crop Management Practices
specificLearningOutcomes: explain management practices carried out on crops
carry out management practices in crop production
appreciate importance of various management practices in crop production
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we carry out management practices in crop production?
learningExperiences: watch a video, or a demonstration on management practices (gapping, thinning, weeding, earthing-up)
carry out selected management practices (gapping, thinning, weeding through physical methods, earthing-up)
make class presentations on the importance of the selected management practices in crop production
linkedLearningAreas: Mathematics: plant spacing and population that guide gapping and thinning relate to measurement and numbers.

subStrands.name: 2.3 Preparing Animal Products: Eggs and Honey
specificLearningOutcomes: explain how to prepare animal products for various purposes
prepare animal products for various purposes
embrace preparation of animal products for various purposes
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we prepare animal products?
learningExperiences: search for information, discuss and share experiences on how to prepare eggs and honey for use and storage
prepare eggs (sorting, grading, packing) and honey (crushing and straining method, packing in appropriate containers)
display prepared animal products and adopt the practice at home and in school
linkedLearningAreas: Pre-Technical Studies: presentation of products for marketing.

subStrands.name: 2.4 Cooking: Grilling, Roasting and Steaming
specificLearningOutcomes: describe methods of cooking different types of foods
cook food using various methods
appreciate the use of varied methods of cooking food
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should we use different methods of cooking food?
learningExperiences: use digital resources, print materials or resource person to source for information on grilling, roasting and steaming foods
use grilling, steaming and roasting methods to prepare foods while observing safety of self and others
make class presentations on the use of varied methods of cooking food
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science: cooking methods relate to transfer of heat.

subStrands.name: 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals
specificLearningOutcomes: describe hygiene practices in rearing domestic animals
carry out hygiene practices in rearing domestic animals
appreciate importance of hygiene practices in rearing domestic animals
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we maintain hygiene while rearing animals?
learningExperiences: search for information on hygienic practices (clean feeders and waterers, clean and well ventilated housing, clean animal) in rearing domestic animals such as pets
carry out appropriate hygiene practices in rearing domestic animals such as cleaning feeders, waterers, cleaning animal structures
make class presentation on the importance of hygiene in rearing domestic animals
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies: animal production as an economic activity.

subStrands.name: 3.2 Laundry: Loose Coloured Items
specificLearningOutcomes: describe how to launder a loose coloured article for hygiene purpose
launder a loose coloured article for hygiene purposes
embrace laundering of loose coloured article for hygiene purposes
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you launder a loose coloured article for hygienic purposes?
learningExperiences: watch a video clip or a demonstration on how to launder a loose coloured item (sorting, washing by kneading and squeezing, drying, finishing)
launder a loose coloured item (sorting, washing by kneading and squeezing, drying, finishing)
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts: tie and dye technique of fixing colours.

subStrands.name: 4.1 Sewing Skills: Knitting
specificLearningOutcomes: describe knitting stitches used in making household articles
knit various articles for household use
embrace knitted articles for household use
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you knit an article for household use?
learningExperiences: use digital devices or real materials or print media to identify basic knitting stitches (purl and knit)
knit a simple household article such as a tools bag, scarf, gloves, mats or table wipers

subStrands.name: 4.2 Constructing Framed Suspended Garden
specificLearningOutcomes: describe framed suspended garden for growing crops
construct a framed structure for suspended garden
embrace the use of framed suspended garden for growing crops
keyInquiryQuestions: How are framed suspended gardens constructed?
learningExperiences: search for photos, videos and illustrations on framed suspended gardens to describe how they are constructed
innovate and construct framed suspended gardens using locally available materials such as wires, wooden planks, metal bars and poles
establish a crop on the constructed framed suspended garden
linkedLearningAreas: Pre-Technical Studies: drawing, designing and use of related tools.

subStrands.name: 4.3 Adding Value to Crop Produce
specificLearningOutcomes: explain ways of adding value on crop produce
add value to a selected crop produce
appreciate the importance of value addition on crop produce
keyInquiryQuestions: Why do we add value to crop produce?
How can we add value to crop produce?
learningExperiences: discuss ways of adding value to crop produce such as potatoes, cassava, groundnuts, simsim, sweet potatoes and pumpkin
process a provided sample of crop produce such as potatoes, cassava, groundnuts, simsim, sweet potatoes and pumpkin to add value using appropriate methods like drying and frying
compare the processed crop produce to raw crop produce in terms of monetary value and storage life

subStrands.name: 4.4 Making Homemade Soap
specificLearningOutcomes: identify the forms of soap used at household level
make homemade soap using natural ingredients
embrace homemade soap for household use
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we make soap using natural ingredients?
learningExperiences: brainstorm and share experiences on forms of soap (liquid, cake/bar, paste, powder) used at household level
use natural ingredients such as ashes, salt, water, animal fats or plant oils to make soap
use the homemade soap for cleaning purposes
linkedLearningAreas: Integrated Science: recycling and reusing wastes.
